name: ECDSA specifics: malleability, zero-address ecrecover, and domain separation
requires: an ecrecover or ECDSA.recover site gating a value-moving action
a signed message or digest the protocol assembles itself
no nonce, or a nonce the attacker can influence
questions: Is the address returned by ecrecover compared against address(0) before it is trusted as a signer?
Is s constrained to the lower half of the curve order, or does the protocol accept both malleable forms?
Does recovery happen against a digest the protocol built itself, and does that digest bind this contract and this chain or only the payload?
Is the nonce part of the signed payload, and is it consumed exactly once before any value moves?
Can the same signature be replayed on a second contract, or a forked chain, that shares this digest construction?
Is the hash built with abi.encodePacked over two dynamic types, where a length collision can be forced?
Does the signed struct hash omit any field that the executor later reads when it moves value?
Is the signer a single EOA or an owner set, and who can mutate that set while a signature is outstanding?
false_positives: OpenZeppelin ECDSA.recover is used, which rejects s above half-order and address(0)
The digest carries a full EIP-712 domain separator and a consumed nonce
The contract is the only one that can verify this digest
The signature is single-use by an on-chain record
poc_must_show: the same signature accepted twice, or on two contracts, with both results shown
a control run where the nonce is consumed and the replay must revert
the ecrecover-returns-zero case if it is the defect, printed
impact_bar: Reportable when a signature can be replayed or forged to move value, quantified. Informational for missing malleability hardening where replay is already blocked by a nonce.
